tagline: Leading independent oil and gas producer focused on highest return, lowest cost operations with strong reserves replacement and sustainable long-term energy development
hero_kpi_rationale: Proved reserves of 5,514 MMBoe represent the foundational asset of an E&P company, with growth of 766 MMBoe (+12% YoY) reflecting success in reserves additions, a key criterion for long-term viability and growth
company_description: EOG Resources, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, explores for, develops, produces, and markets crude oil, natural gas liquids, and natural gas in producing basins in the United States, the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago, and internationally. The company also offers crude oil and condensate, and gathering, processing and marketing. The company was formerly known as Enron Oil & Gas Company. EOG Resources, Inc. was incorporated in 1985 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas.

risks.title: Commodity Price Volatility
risks.summary: Fluctuations in oil and gas prices significantly impact EOG's revenues, earnings, and cash flows.
risks.score_rationale: EOG is directly exposed to oil and gas price volatility. In 2025, NYMEX crude prices declined 14% to $64.78/barrel while gas increased 51% to $3.43/MMBtu, directly impacting revenues and net income (down 22%).

risks.title: Reserves Management and Replacement
risks.summary: The ability to identify, develop, and replace proved reserves is critical for operational continuity and long-term growth.
risks.score_rationale: EOG's long-term viability depends on its ability to maintain and replace reserves. Although reserves increased 12% in 2025 (766 MMBoe), a prolonged decline would threaten future operations.

risks.title: Geopolitical and Regulatory Risks
risks.summary: International operations and the regulatory environment expose EOG to geopolitical and compliance risks.
risks.score_rationale: EOG operates in the United States (99% of reserves), Trinidad (1%), and new projects in Bahrain and the UAE. Political changes, sanctions, or regulatory modifications can impact resource access and profitability.

risks.title: Environmental and Energy Transition Risks
risks.summary: Operational environmental risks and the global energy transition could impact future demand and operations.
risks.score_rationale: As an oil and gas producer, EOG is exposed to operational environmental risks (spills, accidents) and long-term risks from the transition to a low-carbon economy.

risks.title: Market and Demand Risks
risks.summary: Changes in global demand, trade policies, and competition impact EOG's profitability.
risks.score_rationale: Global oil and gas demand is subject to changes due to economic, technological, and political factors, as well as trade policies (tariffs, trade barriers mentioned in the 10-K).

risks.title: Liquidity and Capital Structure
risks.summary: EOG maintains a disciplined capital structure but is increasing debt following the Encino acquisition, raising interest rate exposure.
risks.score_rationale: Although EOG has a strong liquidity position ($3.4B cash + $3.0B credit facility), the $4.5B debt issuance (4 tranches in July and November 2025) for the Encino acquisition increases financial leverage and exposure to future interest rates.
